fluff.overview: The Hong Lung Interdiction Station is a compact orbital defense platform commissioned by the Capellan Confederation in 3024, purpose-built to prevent prisoner escapes from the penal moon of Brazen Heart in the Brighton system. Developed by the Capellan Science Foundation for a very specific tactical requirement, the design prioritizes threat neutralization and vessel capture over sustained combat endurance. At 2,000 tons and roughly 60 meters in diameter, the Hong Lung is among the smallest purpose-built space stations documented in the Inner Sphere, yet its symmetrical armament and dedicated marine boarding capability make it a credible threat to any civilian or lightly armed vessel regardless of approach angle. Every aspect of the station's design reflects its original mission: stopping ships, not destroying them, and ensuring the return of unauthorized escapees to custody.
fluff.capabilities:
The Hong Lung's defensive layout is identical across all six firing arcs, ensuring consistent coverage against escape attempts from any direction. Each arc mounts a quad-mounted PPC battery for long-range hull strikes capable of disabling drive systems, a paired LRM-20 battery providing sustained interdiction fire at medium range, and a bank of six medium lasers for close-defense against small craft and assault shuttles attempting to bypass the station. This arrangement produces eighteen weapon bays in total, with the matched configuration ensuring no approach vector offers reduced exposure to the station's weapons. Seventy-nine single heat sinks provide adequate thermal management for defensive engagements, though simultaneous full fire across all facings exceeds the station's dissipation capacity. Fifty-three points of standard aerospace armor are distributed evenly across the hull's six facings, a practical choice for an omnidirectional threat environment, though the overall protection level reflects the station's mass constraints.

Two assault shuttles housed in the station's small craft bay are kept ready to transport the marine complement aboard disabled vessels, with cargo space supporting the logistics of sustained orbital operations. The Hong Lung's designers assessed the design as a match for a military-grade Union-class DropShip in a direct engagement, reflecting confidence in its concentrated firepower. Its principal limitation is its complete inability to maneuver: with no propulsion capability, the station cannot reposition to cover orbital gaps, and a determined attacker capable of exploiting geometry outside a single arc's coverage could reduce the effectiveness of its otherwise formidable armament.
fluff.deployment: The Hong Lung entered service in 3024 in orbit above Brazen Heart, the prison moon of Brighton IV in the Capellan Confederation's St. Ives Commonality. With no propulsion capability, each station occupied a fixed orbital position assigned to provide overlapping coverage across the moon's primary approach corridors. The original four completed stations were distributed to maintain mutual fire support, each covering a segment of the orbital envelope while relying on neighboring platforms to address gaps in coverage. Following the Confederation's reclamation of the St. Ives Compact, the surviving three stations resumed their orbital watch above Brazen Heart, positioned to cover approach corridors with reduced overlap compared to the original four-station configuration.
fluff.history:
The Hong Lung's origins lie in the personal security concerns of Chancellor Maximilian Liao, whose frequent visits to Brazen Heart had convinced him that the moon's prisoner population represented a persistent escape risk, given the number of supply ships regularly touching down on the surface. His solution was characteristically direct: in 3022, he ordered the Capellan Science Foundation to design and construct eight interdiction stations to ring the moon, each capable of disabling any vessel attempting to depart without authorization. The CSF drew on aging capital system defense station records from the Star League era as their design baseline, adapting the broad concept to the Confederation's available technology and production capacity. The prototype was declared operational above Brazen Heart's northern polar cap in 3024, with follow-on construction proceeding over the following years.

By the time the Davion invasion that triggered the Fourth Succession War reached full intensity, three additional Hong Lungs had been built beyond the prototype. The war effort and the subsequent secession of the St. Ives Commonality brought further construction to a halt before the planned complement of eight could be completed. The St. Ives military mothballed the existing stations when the Brazen Heart penal facility was closed in the 3030s, leaving them in low orbit above an abandoned moon. Three of the four completed stations survived intact to the reclamation of the St. Ives Compact by the Capellan Confederation, at which point the Maskirovka arranged for all surviving stations to be reactivated.

Following reactivation, the Confederation turned its attention to what further use might be made of the design. A feasibility assessment team dispatched from Sian arrived in the Brighton system to evaluate the Hong Lungs as close-orbit planetary defense platforms, extending their utility beyond the prison-moon role they had been built to fill. Proposals circulating through the Strategios suggested constructing upgraded versions as part of the Xin Sheng reconstruction effort, potentially adapting the design for a broader defensive role across Capellan space.
